text: HTTPS is the foundation of web security, encrypting data between the user’s browser and the server so that sensitive information cannot be intercepted. Authentication ensures that only authorised users can access certain parts of a website, often through passwords or two-factor verification. However, even with strong login systems, developers must validate all user input before processing it. This means checking that fields like email addresses or search boxes contain only expected data. Without proper validation, attackers can exploit common vulnerabilities such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting (XSS), where malicious code is injected into forms or URLs. By combining HTTPS, careful authentication, and rigorous input checks, developers can significantly reduce these risks and build safer applications.
